text:
maya: Quick sync — we need a lean battlecard for next week's LLM Ops webinar. Focus: "serving vs owning" (latency, cost, reliability) against cloud AI platforms and LLM API vendors. Who owns claims + 3 field-ready soundbites? Need by EOD Tue.

jamie: I'm on it. Quick Q — audience is SDRs + AE field or deeper product folks?

maya: Mostly SDRs/AEs for lead followup + a short slide for webinar panelists (so 2 formats: talking bullets + a 1-slide claim).

rachel: Proposed framing — 1) Predictable latency at scale (we route + reserve capacity) 2) Unit economics controls (batching, quant profiles) 3) Graceful degradation (fallback models/regions). Short soundbites:
- "Serving is your moat: consistent latency, predictable cost." 
- "Cut token spend without retraining — batching + cache." 
- "Fallbacks keep revenue flowing when clouds saturate."

tony: For field use add a quick bench claim + an objection handler. Bench idea: p95/responses for typical chat prompt at 2k tokens: Redwood Dedicated: 450-600ms, Managed cloud endpoints: 700-1.2s (use internal benchmark link). Objection handler snippet:
- Prospect: "Can't we just use cloud endpoints?"
- SDR: "Yes, for dev & small scale. For production we help you hit latency SLAs and predictable cost — fewer surprises on monthly bills."

ops-bot: Latest_internal_bench_report -> https://redwood.internal/bench/2026-03-serving-summary (internal)

maya: Nice. Can we compress those into 1-line web copy + 3 quick rebuttals for SDR card? Draft below — please edit:

```
Web headline: "Serve LLMs like a product — predictable latency, lower unit cost, and graceful fallbacks."
SDR hooks (3):
1) "We reduce p95 latency variance — customers see faster responses at scale."
2) "Smart batching & caching lower your token bill without retraining models."
3) "When clouds fail, your app stays live via model fallbacks & smart routing."

Objection handlers:
- "We already have cloud infra." -> "Cloud is great for experiments; Redwood makes production predictable and cheaper per token."
- "How do you measure cost savings?" -> "We show token-level cost breakdowns and test runs; typical customers see 15-40% unit savings depending on workload."
```

jamie: Love the SDR hooks. Quick edit on #2: change to "reduce effective token spend" — less jargon.

rachel: I'm going to craft the one-slide claim & a printable 6-line battlecard. Assigning the battlecard draft to me, will post by Mon noon.

tony: I'll pull the p95/p50 numbers for 3 representative workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings) and PR the mini-bench table into the doc.

maya: Perfect. Owner list:
- rachel -> battlecard draft (Mon 12:00)
- tony -> bench numbers + appendix (Mon 17:00)
- jamie -> SDR soundbite polish + objection scripts (Tue 09:00)

Please add any compliance phrasing if needed (PCI/HIPAA). If no objections, we'll lock copy Wed morning and hand off to design.

rachel: noted on compliance. I'll cc security for HIPAA line: "supports customer-managed keys & VPC controls." 

maya: Thanks all — this thread will be the single source. Ping me if you need a faster turn. :rocket:
